title: Corneal abrasion from contact lens
notes: Needs eye exam only, discharged with prescription. No resources.

input.complaint: I was taking my contacts out last night and I think I scratched my cornea. The light really bothers my eyes. My right eye is red and tearing.

title: Medication overdose with respiratory depression
notes: RR 10, SpO2 86% — cannot protect airway, needs intubation. SpO2 < 90 should fire A5.

input.complaint: EMS brought in this 18-year-old found lethargic and not acting right by her roommates. History of depression. Multiple superficial lacerations to both wrists. She is barely breathing.

title: Self-inflicted gunshot wound to head, intubated

input.complaint: EMS arrived with an unresponsive 19-year-old male with a single self-inflicted gunshot wound to the head. He was intubated by EMS. Before intubation his Glasgow Coma Scale was 3.

title: Blood pressure medication refill
notes: Prescription refill, BP controlled, no complaints. No resources.

input.complaint: I ran out of my blood pressure medicine and my doctor is on vacation. Can someone here write me a prescription? No other complaints.

title: Bicycle fall, wrist pain plus elbow laceration
notes: Needs X-ray of wrist AND suture of elbow laceration = 2 resources.

input.complaint: I fell off my bike and landed on my right arm. I have pain in my wrist area and a 2-centimeter laceration on my left elbow. My helmet saved me.

title: Shortness of breath, smoker on birth control
notes: RR 32, SpO2 93%, smoker on BCP — high risk for PE. Handbook says ESI 2.

input.complaint: I have had shortness of breath for several hours. I am a smoker and I take birth control pills.

title: Near-drowning, child unresponsive
notes: 4-year-old near-drowning, breathing spontaneously but unresponsive. A7 should fire.

input.complaint: My 4-year-old was pulled out of the family pool by a neighbor who gave mouth-to-mouth. The child is now breathing on his own but continues to be unresponsive.

title: Child with abdominal pain and vomiting
notes: 7-year-old, abdominal workup needs labs + CT/ultrasound = 2 resources.

input.complaint: My son woke up with a stomach ache. He refused to walk downstairs and is not interested in eating or playing. He just vomited.
I was running across the playground and fell. I have a cut over my right knee. Immunizations are up to date.

title: Wrist injury after slipping on ice
notes: Needs X-ray to rule out fracture = 1 resource. Splint is not a resource.

input.complaint: I slipped on the ice and I hurt my wrist. There is no obvious deformity.

title: Child fall with loss of consciousness
notes: 4-year-old, witnessed fall with LOC, change in consciousness. High risk.

input.complaint: My 4-year-old fell off the jungle gym at preschool, about a 4 foot fall. A witness says she hit her head and was unconscious for a couple of minutes. She is crying and asking for me. Her left arm is splinted.

title: Suspected urinary tract infection
notes: Dysuria and frequency, no abdominal pain. Needs urinalysis = 1 resource (lab).

input.complaint: I think I have a urinary tract infection. I have burning when I urinate and I am going frequently. No abdominal pain or vaginal discharge.

title: Febrile neonate, 2 weeks old
notes: T 101F (38.3C) in infant < 28 days. Must be ESI 2 regardless of appearance.

input.complaint: My pediatrician told me to bring him in because of his fever. He is 2 weeks old, an uncomplicated vaginal delivery, and is otherwise acting appropriately.

title: Motor vehicle crash with shock
notes: Unrestrained driver, 45 mph, BP 74/50, HR 132, RR 36 — signs of shock. ESI 1.

input.complaint: Paramedics arrived with a 16-year-old unrestrained driver who hit a tree at about 45 miles per hour. The passenger side had significant damage. He was moaning but moving all extremities. He looks pale.

title: Smoke inhalation with airway compromise
notes: Hoarse, sore throat, working hard to breathe after smoke inhalation. Handbook says ESI 1 (likely needs intubation). May reveal a gap if our engine returns ESI 2 via B42.

input.complaint: The smoke was so bad I just couldn't breathe. I went into my burning apartment to rescue my cat. I am hoarse, my throat is sore, and I am coughing. I am working hard to breathe. I have asthma.
